newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso recovers from Brazil, local rates help.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso recovers from Brazil, local rates help.

text.p: The Mexican peso recouped much of the ground it had lost during the prior session at the close of trade on Wednesday after investors switched from dollars to the local money market while U.S. long bond yields dipped, traders said.
"Locals were very long on dollars after Brazil rattled us yesterday, thinking the peso would weaken further, but you can't keep the peso down with rates this high," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended the session 4.5 and 3.1 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8750/7.8800 and 7.8870/7.8910 per dollar.
Overnight Cetes rates in the secondary market were down 65 basis points on demand to 20.35 percent in late secondary market trading.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds had meanwhile gained 26/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
Dealers said a recovery by the Sao Paulo blue chip Bovespa index, up 6.25 percent to 12,343 points, also prompted local players to shed long dollar positions they had acquired on Tuesday.
Traders noted that a recovery by peso futures in Chicago MEX02 also helped restore confidence on the Mexican foreign exchange market.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 4.5 centavos weaker at 7.9220/7.9250 per dollar after lagging behind the market.
Peso contracts could gather more strength on Thursday, traders said, if investors chose to switch to peso instruments prior to the weekend.
